reuse.why: Adds a shared isDailyWeekendSkip predicate and lookahead constant in shared/schedules.ts and uses them from getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the budget schedule template, still relying on getDateWithSkippedWeekend for the move case.

duplication.why: The act of skipping weekend occurrences (take a 7x lookahead, drop d.isWeekend dates) is written twice, as a find in getNextDate and as filter+slice in getUpcomingDates, rather than in one helper.

placement.why: The rule predicate lives in shared/schedules.ts next to getNextDate/getDateWithSkippedWeekend, and frequency is plumbed through parseRecurDate where schedule data is built; schedule-template reaching in via a computed noSkipWeekend flag is the one awkward spot.

scope.why: All edits serve the daily-skip rule and its tests.

maintainability.why: Reasonable but the rule is split: callers must know to combine isDailyWeekendSkip with getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag (schedule-template inverts it) and getUpcomingDates re-implements the skip, so a future change touches several places.

bypasses_abstraction.where: app.ts getUpcomingDates filters weekend occurrences itself instead of going through getNextDate/a shared skip helper; schedule-template.ts still applies getDateWithSkippedWeekend on its own after getNextDate

disguised_duplication.where: weekend-occurrence skipping appears as a find over a 7-occurrence lookahead in getNextDate and as take count*7 + filter + slice in getUpcomingDates

one_place.where: whether the rule applies is one predicate (isDailyWeekendSkip), but the skipping itself is implemented separately in shared getNextDate and server getUpcomingDates, and schedule-template decides via its own noSkipWeekend computation
